original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: For eight read-only F2 sources and 70 distinct dirty outputs indexed by all four-subsets, test whether a restored 16-toggle source word consisting of two complete sweeps has prefix differences covering every weight-four mask. Fix the first sweep by relabelling symmetry and exhaust all 8! second-sweep orders.
scope_change_reason: The selector card proposed adding one connector operation, but the live connector alphabet queue is crowded by pair-source DUO (#2128), the active GF(4) scalar-source claim (#2262), and seven-source low-weight masks plus an extra-pair search (#2229 and Discussion #2221). This cycle changes the output family and parameter domain instead: keep the established singleton alphabet and test the previously unrepresented eight-source weight-four shell. Exact current overlap searches for eight-source weight-four and four-subset source words returned no direct match.
bottleneck_link: A short shared source path can lower complete-call cost for a restricted decoder mask family. The result is a connector-level mechanism only; it is not an admitted recursive supplier or a selected-kappa change.
stop_rule: Enumerate exactly all 8! second-sweep permutations after fixing the first sweep to 0..7. For each path compute its 17 prefix parities and exact pairwise-difference coverage of all 70 four-subsets. Stop at the first full cover; if none, exhaust the domain and report the exact maximum and witness. Do not infer impossibility for other 16-toggle words or other source alphabets.
evidence: PASS_TWO_SWEEP_WEIGHT_FOUR_CENSUS: all 40320 permutations exhausted; maximum 23/70 masks, attained by 68 paths. Prefix-pair and direct interval coverage agree for every path. The maximum witness passed 23,552 exhaustive dirty-state scalar replays; one uncovered-mask, one-readout dirty-connector, and omitted-toggle controls passed. Scope is only the fixed-first-sweep two-complete-sweep family.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scope selection, derivation and implementation.

open_questions.question: Can a restored 18-toggle path cover all 70 weight-four masks when one source occurs four times and the other seven occur twice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A positive path would pay 158 complete calls in the same connector model, only two above the 16-toggle source-call floor, and would turn the scoped obstruction into a nearby constructive improvement.
open_questions.first_step: Refresh open PR and Discussion claims, then select a canonical bounded family of interleaved 18-toggle words and test exact prefix-difference coverage before expanding the search.
open_questions.blocked_by: The unrestricted word space is too large for this cycle; the active seven-source extra-pair work must be checked for overlap before choosing a new scope.
